isReachable.description: False for `onPremise`. The Control Plane holds the record for licensing and support and **cannot reach the installation** — it may sit behind a firewall with no inbound route. Every operation assuming reachability must handle absence rather than timing out, and a cell that has not called home for a month is not necessarily broken.

lastContactAt.description: When the site last called out. The only liveness signal for an unreachable cell, and the number a support engineer asks for first.

licenceExpiresAt.description: On-premise only. Licensing cannot be enforced by a Control Plane the site cannot reach, so a signed licence file is verified locally. **An expired licence degrades rather than stops** — a venue whose gates refuse entry because a licence lapsed over a weekend is worse than one running unlicensed until Monday.

participatesInCrossCell.description: False by default for `onPremise`. Redeeming a pass issued elsewhere requires reaching the issuing cell at that moment, and an on-premise site may not be able to. Exclusion is the honest default; local-then-reconcile carries a double-redemption risk that needs a decision rather than an assumption.

deploymentRef.description:
**A pointer to where this cell runs, not a description of it.** A Kubernetes namespace, an ECS cluster ARN, a stack name — whatever the orchestrator calls the thing.

**The platform does not model instances, nodes or shards** (31 August). Kubernetes already holds instance counts and they change by the second; a table copying them drifts within minutes and the copy would win.

**The line is: routing decisions belong to the platform, provisioning facts belong to the orchestrator.** Qdrant is the proof — ADR-0021 makes the tenant *the* shard key, so nine operations route without a lookup and **a stored shard assignment would be a second copy of something derivable.**

**CF-161 needed a table after all, and this said it did not.** The claim here was that one database per cell or one per service is a build-time decision and the DDL is identical either way. **ADR-0038 answered it per tenant**, which drops `Cell.tenantId`, adds `CellTenant`, `RolloutTenant` and a per-tenant migration row, and takes `control` out of the tenant template. `tools/derive-ddl.py` carried the same claim in its docstring.

**A claim that a question cannot affect your artefact is the one most likely to be left standing after it does**, which is why the correction is recorded here rather than the sentence simply deleted.

tenantCount.description: Reported, and **deliberately not the sizing signal.** Forty quiet tenants may load a cell less than three busy ones.

dimensions.description: Per dimension, because the response differs. Short of connections and long on storage is a different problem from short of both.

headroom.description: Fraction remaining. Negative means already over.

forecastBreachAt.description: When the constrained dimension is projected to run out at the current trend. Null where there is no trend to project — an honest null beats an invented date.

schemaVersion.description: From the cell's version register. Skew across a tenant's cells is expected during rollout; unexplained skew is a defect.

CellKind.description:
Four deployment models (ADR-0017). `shared` is the default; the others exist because a client asked or a law requires it.


**`burst` added 31 August.** An environment stood up for one on-sale and torn down after (CF-162 scenario c). **It is not a jurisdiction and it is not permanent** — it holds a catalogue snapshot, three services of sixteen, and 17 tables of 380.

**The other four are places data lives. This one is a place data passes through**, which is why it has its own lifecycle and a reconciliation obligation the others do not.

aggregateCost.description: Combined refresh load of every tile.

refreshSeconds.description: Minimum thirty seconds. A tile refreshing every second is a load problem wearing a convenience costume.

ReportResult.x-ticvai-persistence: none — result set, cached in object storage

dataAsOf.description: Replica position the result was read at. Reporting reads a lag-tolerant replica, so this may trail the primary by seconds — stating it prevents an argument about a figure that moved.

WafRule.description: **Drafted 4 September.** One firewall rule, and the reason it is a row rather than a config file is that somebody has to be able to say who changed it and when.

matchOn.description: What the rule inspects - a path, a header, a source range.

hitCount24h.description: **A rule with no hits is either protecting nothing or blocking everything silently**, and both want looking at.
